heading: Homeland Security Investigations Victim Assistance Program

children.heading: Forensic interview specialist
children.text: The term “forensic interview specialist” is an interview professional who has specialized experience and training in conducting trauma-informed forensic interviews with victims of crime.

children.heading: Victim
children.text: The term “victim” has the meaning given such term in section 20141(e)(2) of title 34.

children.heading: Victim assistance specialist
children.text: The term “victim assistance specialist” is a victim assistance professional who—
has experience working with victims of crime in a service capacity;
has been trained on the exposure of various forms of trauma and other stressors experienced in working with victims; and

may have experience working with local government and community-based organizations, including victim advocacy centers, child advocacy centers, child welfare agencies, faith-based organizations, and other social service programs.

tree.heading: In general
tree.text: There is established, in Homeland Security Investigations of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Victim Assistance Program.

children.text: provide oversight, guidance, training, travel, equipment, and coordination to Homeland Security Investigations victim assistance personnel throughout the United States;
1 forensic interview specialist and 1 victim assistance specialist for each Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent in Charge office;
every Homeland Security Investigations office participating in a human trafficking task force; and
every Homeland Security Investigations office participating in a child sexual exploitation task force;
support Homeland Security Investigations regional attaché offices, to the extent necessary;
provide training regarding victims’ rights, victim-related policies, roles of forensic interviewers and victim assistance specialists, and an approach that is—
linguistically appropriate, to the extent feasible; and

purchase emergency items that are needed to assist identified victims in Homeland Security Investigations criminal investigations, including food, clothing, hygiene products, transportation, and temporary shelter that is not otherwise provided by a nongovernmental organization.

notes.heading: Termination of Section
notes.text: For termination of section by section 6 of Pub. L. 118–96, see Termination Date note below.

notes.heading: Termination Date
notes.text: Section to cease to be effective Oct. 1, 2030, see section 6 of Pub. L. 118–96, set out as a Termination Date of 2024 Amendment note under section 252 of this title.

notes.heading: Investigators Maintain Purposeful Awareness to Combat Trafficking Trauma Program
notes.text: Pub.
